label: Accelerate the free leg and own its return
effort: Sweep the free leg quickly through a low rotational kick and arrest it in a controlled re-chamber before putting it down.
brief: The demand shifts from starting the body to accelerating and recovering the moving thigh. The supporting jobs isolate lateral chamber lift, single-leg upward push, inward sweep, knee-flexor recoil and stance control while the free leg stays raised.
marker: valid E2 attempts out of four per leg with an immediate soft-knee recoil and a two-second re-chamber hold without a rescue touchdown.

e.name: Supported fast lateral chamber lift
e.execution: Use light fingertip bench support. Lift the bent free knee briskly outward to a low roundhouse chamber, keeping the knee folded and the pelvis tall; lower under control. This is a short lift, not a leg swing through end range.
e.job: Accelerate the thigh into the lateral chamber before the lower leg contributes.
e.gate: Reduce lift height instead if the pelvis hikes or the trunk leans; support must remain light.
e.novelty: Rapid frontal-plane chamber lift from the floor, distinct from the sagittal knee drive and already-raised thigh sweep.

e.name: Low roundhouse to suspended re-chamber
e.execution: From a stationary rear-leg kick stance, perform one low roundhouse. Immediately fold the knee and recover the thigh to a low chamber; hold the foot off the floor for 2 s before placing it back in stance. The athlete does not jump.
e.job: Directly train the rapid return and controlled arrest of the kicking leg, rather than allowing it to fall after extension.
e.gate: Use a shorter extension/low chamber instead if the foot drops or the support knee twists; hold quality matters more than range.
e.novelty: Terminal task is active suspended re-chamber, not Class 1 return-to-ground finish or Class 2 no-gather launch.

e.name: Single-leg knee-drive jump to two-foot stick
e.execution: Push vertically from the named leg while driving the other bent knee upward; land softly on two feet and hold 2 s. Keep height controlled and do not turn in flight.
e.job: Coordinate stance-leg extension with free-thigh acceleration while simplifying landing support.
e.gate: Use lower height or a small rear-toe assist at takeoff instead if force production becomes a balance struggle; record assistance.
e.novelty: Unilateral vertical takeoff plus free-knee drive to bilateral landing; no lateral travel, scissor exchange or airborne rotation.

e.name: Low inward crescent shadow sweep
e.execution: With a soft knee, sweep the low free foot from slightly outside toward the midline in a small inward arc, coordinated with a comfortable support-foot/pelvic turn. Finish by folding the knee and placing the foot down. No crossing beyond a controllable midline range.
e.job: Express an inward thigh/adductor sweep that helps recover the leg after rotational extension.
e.gate: Use a bent-knee inward sweep instead at the same dose if the longer lever pulls at the groin; never force a high or locked-knee crescent.
e.novelty: New inward sweeping action, rather than outward roundhouse projection; terminal lever and tissue demand are explicitly limited.

e.name: Supported rapid knee-flexion recoil
e.execution: Stand with fingertip support and the moving thigh nearly vertical. Briskly fold that knee to bring the heel toward the back of the thigh through a comfortable range, then lower slowly. Keep the hip quiet and avoid a ballistic heel strike.
e.job: Isolate knee-flexor acceleration for the folding phase of re-chamber without another whole kick.
e.gate: Use a smaller fold instead for hamstring cramp, back arching or hip swing; symptoms end the task.
e.novelty: Rapid isolated knee flexion; no hip lift, transverse sweep or support exchange.

e.name: Forward support-leg hop with chamber held
e.execution: Hold the free knee in a low bent chamber and make one very short forward hop on the support leg, landing on that same leg with the chamber maintained. Hold 2 s; travel no more than 0.5 m, no turn.
e.job: Keep the supporting leg organized while the other leg remains unavailable to catch bodyweight during recoil.
e.gate: Use a smaller hop or an assisted free-toe touchdown instead if the chamber drops or another hop is needed; record the assistance.
e.novelty: Forward same-leg support task with a suspended free thigh, unlike Class 2 lateral hop with the free leg available.

p_jobs: Maintain stance-leg push without spending extra sets before the chamber-strength emphasis.
Load posterior-chain control that steadies the support hip during free-leg recoil.
Supply adductor/lateral hip capacity for the inward sweep and return to stance.
Maintain a controlled hip-turn strength contribution while reducing its set share from Class 3.
Main strength investment: active chamber lifting and controlled lowering, separate from rapid recoil skill.
Support the flexed-knee ankle base while the free leg is suspended.
s_jobs: Airplane work reinforces pelvic control during a raised-leg task; short-foot holds support the forefoot base without adding calf fatigue.
readiness: The coach must qualify low suspended-chamber balance and a pain-free inward arc. No high crescent, locked-knee kick, repeated snap or fast stretch is prescribed. If recoil cannot be controlled, reduce the lever/height inside the same slot.
strength_reason: Class 3 allocated two rounds to hip internal rotation. Shift that second round to P5 hip flexion: [1,1,1,1,2,1], still 92 working reps. This is a change in strength job emphasis, not an automatic band-load increase.
exposure_note: Eight flight/landings: four unilateral takeoffs to bilateral landings plus four same-leg hop landings. Twenty grounded efforts include twelve kick/sweep actions; the re-chamber hold is part of each kick, not an extra rep.
space: Keep vertical jumps in a cleared footprint, hops within 0.5 m and kick sweeps below hip height with clear space all around; retain at least 2 m recovery clearance in the 10 m lane.
progression: After held-start work, the new learning objective is active free-leg recovery. Total landings stay at eight, with four now unilateral; that redistribution needs independent landing qualification and is not an inferred progression pass.
audit: A second full roundhouse variant was avoided: the supporting drills separate thigh lift, inward sweep, knee folding and stance control. Only four inward sweeps are prescribed, with a shorter-lever replacement. The main kick stops in a low re-chamber rather than an extreme end position.
authoring_handoff: Review Class 4 and actual hip/adductor response before Class 5, then design lateral arrival into rotational force; audit/save Class 5 before continuing.
current_handoff: Record actual delivery/response and review the next saved class against readiness.
